articles.headline: OFAC Announces Settlement with Pegasus Worldwide Logistics, Designates International Criminal Court, and Removes Burma-Related Designation
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced a settlement agreement with Pegasus Worldwide Logistics. This action is part of OFAC's ongoing efforts to enforce sanctions compliance across various sectors.

In a separate but concurrent action, OFAC designated entities related to the International Criminal Court (ICC) and issued corresponding General Licenses. This move signals a significant policy stance regarding the ICC.
Additionally, OFAC removed a Burma-related designation, indicating a recalibration of sanctions against certain entities or individuals associated with Burma.

articles.headline: OFAC Issues New Russia-Related General License
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has issued a new Russia-related General License. This license aims to authorize certain transactions that would otherwise be prohibited under existing sanctions against Russia.

The issuance of this General License suggests a targeted adjustment to the broader Russia sanctions program, potentially to facilitate specific humanitarian efforts, trade in certain goods, or other defined activities.
Details of the authorized activities and any associated conditions are outlined within the newly published license, providing clarity for entities engaging in Russia-related transactions.

articles.headline: OFAC Imposes New Iran-Related Designations, Issues General License, and Amends Russia-Related General License
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new Iran-related designations, targeting entities and individuals deemed to be supporting illicit activities of the Iranian regime. These designations are part of ongoing efforts to exert economic pressure on Iran.

Concurrently, OFAC issued a new Iran-related General License, which may permit certain transactions that would otherwise be prohibited under the expanded sanctions. This could indicate specific carve-outs for humanitarian aid or other permitted activities.

Additionally, an existing Russia-related General License was amended, signaling adjustments to the scope of authorized transactions concerning Russia. This amendment reflects the dynamic nature of sanctions policy in response to evolving geopolitical circumstances.

articles.headline: OFAC Removes and Updates Designations, Publishes Iran-Related Alert and Amended FAQ
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced several designations removals and updates, reflecting changes in the status of previously sanctioned entities or individuals. These adjustments are part of OFAC's regular review and maintenance of its sanctions lists.

In a significant development, OFAC published an Iran-related Alert, warning foreign financial institutions (FFIs) that they could be targeted at any time without advance notification for transacting with sanctioned Iranian financial institutions.

Furthermore, an Iran-related Frequently Asked Question (FAQ) was amended, removing language that previously indicated OFAC would generally contact an FFI about its conduct before making a finding of sanctionable activity.

articles.headline: OFAC Imposes New Counter Terrorism Designations
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new designations under its Counter Terrorism sanctions program. These actions target individuals and entities identified as supporting or engaging in terrorist activities globally.
These designations aim to disrupt the financial networks and operational capabilities of terrorist organizations by blocking assets and prohibiting transactions with the designated parties.
The latest designations underscore the U.S. government's ongoing commitment to combating terrorism through financial sanctions and international cooperation.

articles.headline: OFAC Designates Iran-Related Entities and Transnational Criminal Organizations, Issues Determination and Amended FAQ
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new Iran-related designations and updates, targeting entities and individuals involved in activities contrary to U.S. national security and foreign policy interests. These actions are part of a broader strategy to counter the Iranian regime's destabilizing influence.
In a separate action, OFAC also designated entities identified as Transnational Criminal Organizations, aiming to disrupt their illicit financial activities and criminal networks.

Additionally, OFAC published an Iran-related Determination and an Amended Iran-related Frequently Asked Question, providing further guidance and clarification on the scope and implementation of the sanctions.

articles.headline: OFAC Imposes Counter Terrorism and Transnational Criminal Organization Designations, Removes Belarus, Counter Narcotics, and Libya Designations
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new designations under its Counter Terrorism and Transnational Criminal Organizations sanctions programs. These actions target individuals and entities involved in activities that threaten U.S. national security.

Concurrently, OFAC removed several designations related to Belarus, Counter Narcotics, and Libya. These removals indicate a reassessment of the sanctions landscape in these areas, potentially reflecting changes in behavior or policy.
The combination of new designations and removals highlights OFAC's dynamic approach to sanctions, adapting to evolving threats and geopolitical developments.

articles.headline: OFAC Imposes New Counter Narcotics, Counter Terrorism, Iran-Related, and Non-Proliferation Designations
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced a series of new designations across multiple sanctions programs, including Counter Narcotics, Counter Terrorism, Iran-related, and Non-Proliferation. These actions target a broad spectrum of illicit activities and threats to U.S. national security.

The designations aim to disrupt the financial and operational networks of those involved in drug trafficking, terrorism financing, proliferation of weapons of mass destruction, and activities supporting the Iranian regime.
This comprehensive approach underscores the U.S. government's commitment to leveraging financial sanctions to address diverse global threats.

articles.headline: OFAC Publishes Regulatory Amendments, Cuba Sanctions Regulations, New and Amended FAQs, and Cuba-Related Alert
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) published significant regulatory amendments, including updates to the Cuba Sanctions Regulations. These changes reflect ongoing adjustments to U.S. policy towards Cuba.

In conjunction with the regulatory updates, OFAC issued new and amended Cuba-related Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs), providing further guidance and clarification for individuals and entities engaging in Cuba-related transactions.
Additionally, OFAC published a Cuba-related Alert, drawing attention to specific compliance considerations and potential risks associated with transactions involving Cuba.

articles.headline: OFAC Issues Amended Venezuela General Licenses
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has issued amended Venezuela General Licenses. These amendments modify existing authorizations for certain transactions involving Venezuela, which would otherwise be prohibited under U.S. sanctions.

The issuance of amended General Licenses indicates a recalibration of U.S. policy towards Venezuela, potentially to address specific economic or humanitarian concerns, or to encourage certain political developments.
Entities engaging in Venezuela-related activities should review the updated licenses carefully to ensure compliance with the revised authorizations and any new conditions.

articles.headline: Streamlining Export Controls for Drone Exports
body: The Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) is easing export controls on certain Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs or drones) and related parts, components, accessories, attachments, technology, and software under the Export Administration Regulations (EAR). Specifically, this rule: eliminates wind gust tolerance as a parameter for determining UAV controls under the EAR; increases the threshold for national security controls on certain UAVs from an endurance of 30 minutes to an endurance of 3 hours; makes conforming changes to remove national security controls on software and technology associated with UAVs with an endurance less than 3 hours; maintains military end-use and end-user controls on those lower endurance drones and associated software and technology; clarifies Commerce Control List (CCL) controls for certain UAVs specially designed for military use; and removes national security controls on certain specially designed parts, components, accessories, and attachments for such UAVs as they do not provide any significant military or intelligence capabilities.

articles.headline: Implementation of EAR Export Controls on Silencers, Mufflers, and Sound Suppressors; and Other Firearms Related Changes
body: The Department of Commerce (Commerce), Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) is revising the Export Administration Regulations (EAR) and the Commerce Control List (CCL) to appropriately control certain silencers, mufflers, and sound suppressors (sound suppressors) that will no longer be described on the International Traffic in Arms Regulations U.S. Munitions List (USML). This interim final rule (IFR) complements a Department of State interim final rule published elsewhere in this issue of the Federal Register (International Traffic in Arms Regulations: USML Category I Firearm Suppressors (1400-AG11) (State IFR)). This transfer of jurisdiction will reduce the regulatory burden on exports of sound suppressors. This IFR also revises the EAR to allow firearms and related items to be temporarily exported and reexported under a license exception as tools of trade, thereby relieving exporters of the regulatory burden of applying for authorization. Finally, this IFR clarifies which items fall within the scope of the EAR's entry clearance requirements for a temporary import.

articles.headline: Enhanced Favorable Treatment for the United Arab Emirates Under the Export Administration Regulations
body: In this final rule, the Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) amends the Export Administration Regulations (EAR) to provide enhanced favorable treatment for the United Arab Emirates (UAE). Specifically, BIS is removing the UAE from Country Groups D:3 and D:4 and adding the UAE to Country Group A:5. More license exceptions will now be available, including Strategic Trade Authorization (STA) for the UAE Government and approved commercial entities in the UAE. STA will authorize the export, reexport, or transfer (in-country) of military items; certain commercial satellites and spacecraft; and dual-use items useful in, inter alia, oil and gas production, desalination, and civil nuclear power generation. The UAE Government and approved commercial entities will also have license-free access to advanced computing items, consistent with the May 2025 U.S.-UAE Artificial Intelligence Cooperation framework, without compromising U.S. digital infrastructure buildout.
